A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RG-VFM and retain the central objective and intrinsic/extrinsic variants despite the changed title. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original spherical checkerboard generation experiments, including sample-norm statistics, generated distributions, and flow trajectories.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices E–F report original spherical and hyperbolic experiments, material and protein generation results, reproduced baselines, and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The Gaussian objective and intrinsic/extrinsic constructions remain. v2 adds a Laplace variant minimizing geodesic distance instead of its square (Appendix E.4, Equation 27), and adapts MOFFlow, QFlow, and ReQFlow by substituting endpoint-distance rotational losses. These are limited objective adaptations within the existing framework, retaining the application models' other implementation components.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only spherical checkerboard generation. v2 adds hyperbolic checkerboards, metal-organic framework structure prediction using the Boyd et al. dataset, and protein backbone generation using filtered Protein Data Bank structures (Sections 5.1–5.3). This substantially expands geometric and application coverage.

E2.justification: CFM, VFM, and RFM remain the synthetic comparators. New application comparisons include DiffCSP and MOFFlow in Tables 2 and 7, and RFDiffusion, Genie2, FoldFlow2, FrameFlow, QFlow, and ReQFlow in Table 3. MOFFlow, QFlow, and ReQFlow have separately identified published and reproduced results.

E3.justification: The reported spherical protocol changes from uniform to standard-normal/wrapped-normal priors, from Runge–Kutta to Euler integration, and from 5,000 to 10,000 generated samples (v1 Appendix C.1; v2 Appendix E.2). v2 adds Coverage, C2ST, and manifold-distance metrics, plus application protocols specifying MOF matching tolerances and sample counts and protein evaluation lengths and rectified training.

E4.justification: v1 already includes trajectories, unwrapped distributions, and norm histograms. v2 adds comparisons testing Gaussian versus Laplace posterior losses (Appendix E.4, Table 6) and MOFFlow/V-MOFFlow sensitivity to 2–1,000 integration steps on 1,000 test structures (Appendix F.2, Figure 17). These introduce substantive questions about loss choice and numerical sampling sensitivity.

E5.justification: v1 reports descriptive sample-norm means and standard deviations. v2 expands reporting with ± values for C2ST, manifold distance, and protein scRMSD in Tables 1, 3, and 6. Training-seed and repeated-run counts remain unspecified, and the C2ST/scRMSD spreads are not adequately explained; additional repeated experiments cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive quantitative synthetic, Laplace, material, protein, and integration-step results beyond v1's spherical visualizations and norm statistics. For example, Table 2 reports five-sample match rates at stol = 0.5 of 50.14% for V-MOFFlow versus 46.97% for reproduced MOFFlow. Table 3 reports V-ReQFlow designability of 0.980 versus 0.964 for reproduced ReQFlow, but scRMSD of 0.961 versus 0.939. Updated spherical results use changed settings and do not establish same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The original objective derivation and basic Euclidean/non-Euclidean comparison are retained. v2 adds a proof of the normalizer's independence from the mean on homogeneous manifolds, Jacobi-field Definition 4.1, Propositions 4.1–4.3 relating the losses through curvature, and constant-curvature Corollary D.1, with extensive derivations in Appendix D.4.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims a geometric extension of VFM supported by spherical experiments, with molecular applications prospective. v2 adds central claims that a Jacobi-field curvature term explains stronger endpoint supervision and that variationalizing existing material and protein generators consistently improves performance. These substantially broaden the abstract, introduction, and conclusion's contribution claims.

C2.justification: v1 speculates that endpoint supervision explains sharper checkerboard patterns. v2 develops a curvature-based explanation for stronger supervision, acknowledges that C2ST does not consistently favor RG-VFM, and hypothesizes particular benefits from Laplace losses in hyperbolic space. Appendix F.2 also adds the qualification that MOF property-error magnitudes may be too large for meaningful comparisons.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's basic MLP and training description, v2 discloses 10,000 synthetic training samples, sampling clipping, and manifold-aware Euler implementation. Application details include Batch implementation, two RTX A5000 GPUs for MOFs, and four H100 GPUs with approximately 260 training epochs and 10 rectified fine-tuning epochs for proteins. It identifies reused codebases, although several hyperparameters, filtering instructions, and splits remain delegated to cited sources.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around material/protein generators and their partly variational rotational objectives, including MOFFlow and ReQFlow. It also adds recent VFM extensions for mixed data and scientific applications, and geometric references supporting the Jacobi analysis. This extends v1's primarily general flow-matching and Riemannian-distribution positioning.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around theory and applications, with explicit contribution and experimental-goal structures. Much of v1 Section 3.2 moves to v2 Appendix D.2. The geometric, theoretical, and synthetic appendices move from A–C to C–E, accompanied by expanded background, notation and disclosure sections, and a dedicated main-text Jacobi analysis.

P2.justification: v1's combined framework illustration is redrawn and reorganized into v2 Figures 1–2, including a new Jacobi-field diagram. Existing spherical displays are updated, with expanded captions and histogram reference lines, alongside new hyperbolic and Laplace panels. v2 also introduces quantitative result tables, notation tables, and the integration-step plot in Figure 17.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's narrow, mainly visual validation with quantitative experiments, reproduced application baselines, and sensitivity analyses. However, its central Proposition 4.1 identifies an infinitesimal Jacobi variation with a finite endpoint displacement: Appendix D.4 infers equality of linear terms from Taylor expansions agreeing at s = 1, which does not establish the claimed exact identity. Table 3 also gives V-ReQFlow worse scRMSD than reproduced ReQFlow, contrary to the accompanying claim of improvement on both designability and folding RMSD. These substantial evidential gains and new central theoretical/reporting weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
